description:
## Outcome

`jido daemon` starts an optional daemon supervision tree in the foreground. The TUI, `run`, and `eval` do not start or require it.

## Why now

The package spike must prove foreground daemon behavior. The application now has no OTP application module or daemon boundary.

## Work

1. Add `Jido.Cli.Application` and the named `Jido.Cli.Daemon`, `Supervisor`, `Server`, `Client`, and `Protocol` boundaries from `RELEASE_PLAN.md`.
2. Keep the normal application tree small. Start daemon children only for the daemon command.
3. Reserve and validate `jido daemon`, `jido daemon --help`, `status`, and `health` grammar. Transport-backed status and health come in a later task.
4. Start without provider credentials and keep the process attached to the terminal.
5. Add deterministic child-start, start-failure, and clean-stop tests.
6. Keep exit statuses `0`, `1`, and `64` stable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `jido daemon` stays in the foreground until a supported shutdown request.
- [ ] No daemon child starts for the TUI, `run`, `eval`, help, or version commands.
- [ ] Missing provider credentials do not prevent daemon start.
- [ ] A child-start failure is normalized and leaves no partial daemon tree.
- [ ] Service managers can supervise the foreground process.

## Tests

Add application, daemon supervision, and CLI routing tests with injected supervisors. Run `mix quality`, `mix test --cover`, and `mix docs`.

## Non-goals

Do not implement backgrounding, service installation, transport, automatic discovery, or implicit daemon use.
title: Add the optional foreground daemon supervision boundary
